description: Comprehensive security hardening initiative based on a full-codebase security audit covering input sanitization, bounds checking, authentication/authorization, CORS, file upload validation, open redirects, insecure randomness, unbounded queries, and error information leakage. This PRD documents all identified vulnerabilities as user stories for systematic remediation via Ralph AI loops. Priority 1 items are critical/high severity requiring immediate action, Priority 2 are high/medium, Priority 3 are medium, and Priority 4 are low/hardening improvements.

userStories.title: Harden file upload validation across all upload components
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all file upload components to validate file type, size, and sanitize filenames so that attackers cannot upload malicious files or exploit path traversal. Currently FileStorageManager.tsx (line 112) accepts ANY file with NO type or size validation and uses unsanitized file.name directly in the storage path. DailyReports.tsx (line 177) also lacks file type/size validation and uses Math.random() for filename generation. Create a reusable file upload validation utility at src/lib/security/fileUploadValidation.ts with: (1) validateFileUpload() that checks file type against an allowlist, validates file size against a configurable max, and sanitizes the filename by stripping path separators and special characters, (2) generateSecureFilename() that uses crypto.randomUUID() instead of Math.random(), (3) ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES constant with safe MIME types, (4) MAX_FILE_SIZES constant with per-type size limits. Then apply this utility to FileStorageManager.tsx and DailyReports.tsx.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/security/fileUploadValidation.ts exports validateFileUpload, generateSecureFilename, ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES, MAX_FILE_SIZES
validateFileUpload checks file.type against ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES allowlist and rejects unknown types
validateFileUpload checks file.size against MAX_FILE_SIZES limits (default 10MB for documents, 5MB for images)
generateSecureFilename uses crypto.randomUUID() instead of Math.random() and strips path separators from original filename
FileStorageManager.tsx handleFileUpload calls validateFileUpload before uploading and shows error toast on rejection
DailyReports.tsx handleCreateReport validates each photo file before upload using validateFileUpload
DailyReports.tsx uses generateSecureFilename instead of Math.random()-based naming
npm run build passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Created src/lib/security/fileUploadValidation.ts with validateFileUpload, generateSecureFilename, sanitizeFilename, ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES, MAX_FILE_SIZES, ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS. Applied to FileStorageManager.tsx and DailyReports.tsx. Exported from src/lib/security/index.ts.

userStories.title: Strengthen sanitizeInput to handle encoded XSS payloads
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want sanitizeInput() to neutralize HTML-entity-encoded and URL-encoded XSS payloads so that encoded attack vectors like <script> and %3Cscript%3E are blocked. The current implementation in src/lib/security/sanitize.ts (line 51-56) only strips literal < and > characters with a simple regex replace, which is insufficient against encoded payloads. The existing test suite at src/lib/security/__tests__/xssPayloads.test.ts (lines 528-547) documents this as known gaps with TODO comments. Update sanitizeInput to: (1) decode HTML entities before stripping (handle < > & < < etc), (2) decode URL-encoded characters (%3C %3E %22 etc), (3) strip the decoded angle brackets and dangerous characters, (4) handle double-encoding attacks. Also update the test TODOs to verify the fixes work.
acceptanceCriteria: sanitizeInput in src/lib/security/sanitize.ts decodes HTML entities (< > < < etc) before stripping angle brackets
sanitizeInput decodes URL-encoded characters (%3C %3E %22 %27 etc) before stripping
sanitizeInput handles double-encoded payloads (%253C becomes %3C becomes < which is stripped)
sanitizeInput still preserves normal text without angle brackets or encoded characters
The TODO comments in xssPayloads.test.ts lines 528-547 are resolved with passing assertions
All existing sanitize tests continue to pass
npm run build passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Updated sanitizeInput in src/lib/security/sanitize.ts to decode HTML entities and URL-encoded characters before stripping angle brackets. Handles double-encoding attacks. Updated xssPayloads.test.ts to verify fixes.

userStories.title: Add URL validation for open redirect prevention on API-returned URLs
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all window.location.href assignments that use URLs from API responses to validate the URL domain before redirecting so that compromised or malicious API responses cannot redirect users to attacker-controlled sites. Currently multiple components redirect to URLs returned from edge functions without validation: StripePaymentProcessor.tsx (line 56) redirects to data.checkout_url, QuickBooksIntegration.tsx (line 148) redirects to data.auth_url, CalendarIntegration.tsx (lines 114, 135) redirects to data.auth_url, and Pricing.tsx (line 54) redirects to data.url. Create src/lib/security/urlValidation.ts with: (1) validateRedirectUrl() that checks the URL against an allowlist of trusted domains (stripe.com, intuit.com, accounts.google.com, login.microsoftonline.com, the app's own domain), (2) isTrustedDomain() helper, (3) TRUSTED_REDIRECT_DOMAINS constant. Apply validateRedirectUrl to all identified redirect locations.

validateRedirectUrl parses the URL and checks the hostname against TRUSTED_REDIRECT_DOMAINS

validateRedirectUrl rejects protocol-relative URLs (//evil.com)

QuickBooksIntegration.tsx validates data.auth_url before redirect
CalendarIntegration.tsx validates data.auth_url before redirect (both Google and Outlook)
Pricing.tsx validates data.url before redirect

userStories.title: Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() for security-sensitive IDs
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all security-sensitive random value generation to use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() instead of Math.random() so that generated tokens and IDs are not predictable. Currently ClientPortalAccess.tsx (line 107) generates portal access tokens using Math.random() which is cryptographically insecure and predictable. Multiple file upload components also use Math.random() for filename generation. Audit and fix all instances where Math.random() is used for security-adjacent purposes (tokens, access codes, file paths) in src/ directory.
acceptanceCriteria: ClientPortalAccess.tsx uses crypto.randomUUID() for portal access token generation instead of Math.random()
All file upload components in src/ use crypto.randomUUID() for filename generation instead of Math.random()

No Math.random() usage remains in src/ for token, ID, or filename generation (non-UI purposes)

userStories.title: Add pagination and limits to unbounded Supabase queries
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all Supabase select queries to have explicit .limit() or .range() calls so that no single query can return an unbounded number of rows causing memory exhaustion or DoS. Currently multiple services query without limits: analyticsEngine.ts (lines 200-203 and 260-263) queries financial_records and time_entries with select('*') without limit, taskService.ts (line 85-104) queries all tasks without limit, FileStorageManager.tsx (line 66) has limit(100) which is good but many other query sites don't. Add .limit(1000) as a safety cap to all unbounded select queries in src/services/ and src/hooks/ directories. For user-facing list views, use the paginationSchema from src/lib/validation/schemas.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: analyticsEngine.ts financial_records query has .limit(1000) applied
analyticsEngine.ts time_entries query has .limit(1000) applied
taskService.ts tasks query has .limit(500) applied
All .select('*') queries in src/services/ directory have explicit .limit() calls
No new unbounded queries introduced

userStories.title: Add try-catch to all JSON.parse calls on external data
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all JSON.parse() calls on data from localStorage, sessionStorage, or API responses to be wrapped in try-catch blocks so that malformed data cannot crash the application. Currently QuickLeadCapture.tsx (line 89) calls JSON.parse without try-catch on localStorage data, and CookieConsentManager.tsx (line 184) parses savedConsent without error handling. Audit all JSON.parse calls in src/ and wrap any that handle external/stored data in try-catch with appropriate fallback values.

CookieConsentManager.tsx JSON.parse call is wrapped in try-catch with fallback to show consent banner
All JSON.parse calls in src/ on localStorage/sessionStorage data have try-catch wrappers

userStories.title: Add input sanitization to high-risk form submissions
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want the top 10 most security-sensitive forms to use the useSanitizedForm hook or apply sanitizeInput before database mutations so that user input is sanitized before storage. The useSanitizedForm hook exists at src/hooks/useSanitizedForm.ts but is barely used (only in tests). Of 89 files with form submissions and 237 files with database mutations, very few apply sanitization. Priority forms to fix: (1) CreateProject.tsx - project name/description, (2) TeamManagement.tsx - user info, (3) BlogManager.tsx - blog content, (4) CRMContacts.tsx - contact info, (5) CRMLeads.tsx - lead data, (6) DocumentManagement.tsx - document metadata, (7) Subcontractors.tsx - subcontractor info, (8) JournalEntries.tsx - financial descriptions, (9) BillPayments.tsx - payment notes, (10) CompanySettings.tsx - company details. For each, add sanitizeInput() calls on text fields before the Supabase insert/update call.

userStories.title: Consolidate duplicate sanitization utilities
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want a single source of truth for sanitization functions so that developers always use the correct, most secure version. Currently there are duplicate implementations: src/utils/security.ts (lines 57-63) exports sanitizeInput and sanitizeHtml, while src/lib/security/sanitize.ts exports the same function names with different implementations. The src/utils/security.ts version is weaker (simple regex). Consolidate by making src/utils/security.ts re-export from src/lib/security/sanitize.ts, and update all imports of sanitization functions from src/utils/security.ts to use src/lib/security/sanitize.ts instead.

userStories.title: Add maxLength attributes to form input elements
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all text input and textarea elements in forms to have maxLength HTML attributes matching their Zod schema limits so that client-side bounds are enforced in addition to server-side validation. Currently only 14 of 89+ form files set maxLength on inputs. While Zod schemas define max lengths (100 for names, 255 for emails, 5000 for messages), the HTML inputs lack corresponding maxLength attributes. Add maxLength to inputs in the top 15 most used forms: Auth SignUpForm, Auth SignInForm, CreateProject, CRMContacts, CRMLeads, EstimateForm, DailyReports, TeamManagement, CompanySettings, UserProfile, BlogPostFormDialog, LeadCaptureForm, ContactSalesModal, SafetyIncidentForm, PermitForm.

userStories.title: Add bounds to search schema filters and unbounded record types
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want the searchSchema in src/lib/validation/schemas.ts to have bounded filters so that attackers cannot send thousands of filter parameters causing performance degradation. Currently line 131-139 defines filters as z.record(z.string()).optional() with no bounds on the number of entries or value lengths. Update to z.record(z.string().max(200)).refine(obj => Object.keys(obj).length <= 20) to limit to 20 filters of max 200 chars each. Also audit other z.record() usages in the codebase for similar unbounded patterns.

userStories.title: Sanitize error messages in edge function responses
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all edge function error responses to return generic error messages instead of raw error.message so that internal system details (database schema, file paths, connection strings) are not leaked to clients. Currently multiple edge functions return raw error messages: generate-risk-assessment/index.ts (line 169), save-robots-txt/index.ts (line 54), projects/index.ts (line 40), blog-ai-automation/index.ts (line 131), and many others. For each function in supabase/functions/, replace error.message in response bodies with generic messages like 'An error occurred' while logging the detailed error server-side with console.error.

userStories.title: Replace wildcard CORS with origin validation in edge functions
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all edge functions to use origin-validated CORS headers instead of Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * so that cross-origin requests are restricted to trusted domains only. Currently the majority of edge functions in edge-functions-template/functions/ define local corsHeaders with '*' for the origin. A secure CORS utility exists at edge-functions-template/functions/_shared/secure-cors.ts that validates origins against a whitelist. Update at least 15 of the most sensitive edge functions (auth-related, payment, data mutation) to use getCorsHeaders() from secure-cors.ts instead of hardcoded '*' headers.

userStories.title: Strengthen returnTo parameter validation for open redirect prevention
